questions.corrige_markdown:
**Photosynthesis** is the **process by which green plants (and some other organisms with chlorophyll) manufacture organic food (carbohydrates such as glucose) from simple inorganic substances, carbon dioxide and water, using light energy absorbed by chlorophyll, with oxygen released as a by-product.**

$$\mathrm{6\,CO_2 + 6\,H_2O \xrightarrow[chlorophyll]{light\ energy} C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6\,O_2}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: State the ways in which the leaf is adapted for photosynthesis. *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. The leaf is **broad and flat**, giving a **large surface area** to absorb light and carbon dioxide.
2. It is **thin**, so light penetrates to all the cells and gases have a **short diffusion distance**.
3. The **cuticle and the epidermis are transparent**, so light passes through to the mesophyll.
4. The **palisade mesophyll cells** are **closely packed, upright and contain many chloroplasts**, placed near the upper surface where light intensity is highest.
5. The **chloroplasts contain chlorophyll** which absorbs light energy.
6. The **spongy mesophyll cells are loosely arranged with large air spaces**, so carbon dioxide diffuses easily to the cells and oxygen diffuses out.
7. The **stomata (many, mostly on the lower surface)** open to allow the entry of carbon dioxide and the exit of oxygen; the **guard cells** control their opening.
8. The **veins (xylem and phloem)** bring water and mineral salts to the cells and carry away the sugar made; they also support the leaf.
9. The **waxy cuticle** reduces the loss of water, and the leaf blade is held at a good angle to the light by the **petiole**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Outline the fate of the end products of photosynthesis. *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The end products of photosynthesis are **glucose** (a simple sugar) and **oxygen**.

**Fate of glucose**

1. Some glucose is **used in respiration** in the cells to release energy for the activities of the plant.
2. Some is **converted to starch** and **stored** in the leaves (temporarily), and in the roots, stems, seeds and fruits (permanent storage); starch is insoluble and does not affect the osmotic balance of the cells.
3. Some is **converted to sucrose** (soluble) and **transported in the phloem** to other parts of the plant (growing points, fruits, storage organs).
4. Some is used to make **cellulose**, which forms new **cell walls** (growth).
5. Some is used to make **fats and oils** (stored in seeds and fruits).
6. Some is combined with **nitrates and other mineral salts** from the soil to make **amino acids and proteins** (for growth and enzymes), and **chlorophyll**.

**Fate of oxygen**

1. Some oxygen is **used in respiration** by the plant cells.
2. The rest **diffuses out through the stomata** into the atmosphere, where it is used by animals and other organisms for respiration.
